Reliable TypeScript Boundaries

Static types describe assumptions inside a program, but values arriving from storage, network responses, browser messages, and parsed documents remain unknown until runtime code validates their actual structure.

A small boundary validator should reject malformed data and return a narrow domain type. Keeping this work near the boundary allows the rest of the application to remain direct, readable, and confidently typed.

Prefer discriminated messages

Message objects benefit from a stable type field because each context can select the relevant operation before validating its payload. This also makes logs and tests easier to understand when a workflow crosses several extension contexts.

Validation should cover nested data rather than merely recognizing the outer message name. Otherwise a malformed payload can pass the guard and undermine exactly the safety that the domain model was intended to provide.
